rgb: This indoor room has an exposed ceiling grid, a pale couch with cushions approximately 1.2 to 1.5 metres ahead of the camera wearer, a lamp partly shown along the right edge at about 1.5 metres, and a rear wall with a dark door roughly 4 to 5 metres away on the right. A woman wearing dark glasses and a green quilted jacket sits in the centre of the couch, around 1.0 to 1.2 metres directly ahead. She faces the camera wearer, with her head and gaze angled slightly downward at a vertical blue game grid between them, approximately 0.5 to 0.7 metres from the camera. Both people can reach the grid with an arm. Its lower section and supporting surface, together with the woman's lower body, are cut off by the frame's bottom edge, and the board blocks the lower central part of her torso. From frames 1 through 4, the camera angles slightly downward, exposing more of the grid's upper rows. The woman moves slightly forward from about 1.2 metres to 1.0 metre in frame 3 and lifts her right hand, which holds a yellow disc, just over the grid's left side, before dropping her right arm to the board's left in frame 4. In frame 5, she shifts slightly backward onto the couch, with both arms lowered behind the board. At the same time, the camera wearer's left arm and hand appear from the lower-left foreground at about 0.3 to 0.5 metres, holding a red disc over the grid's upper-left edge and partly obscuring the left couch cushion and the woman's right side.
depth: The monocular depth image separates the indoor setting into distinct distance bands. In the foreground, roughly 0.3 to 0.7 metres away and reachable by both the camera wearer and the opponent, a vertical, perforated Connect Four board occupies the bottom centre and rises farther into view between frames 1 and 4. In frame 5, the camera wearer's left arm and hand enter from the bottom left while holding a red token, forming the brightest and closest surface at approximately 0.2 to 0.4 metres. Immediately behind the board, about 0.9 to 1.3 metres from the camera wearer and 0.3 to 0.5 metres behind the board, a woman in dark glasses and a puffy jacket sits facing forward on a couch and looks down toward the board separating them. Couch cushions spread behind her on both sides at about 1.2 to 1.8 metres, and a floor lamp stands at the extreme right edge around 2.0 metres away. Over the five frames, the camera wearer's viewpoint tilts downward and shifts slightly nearer the table from frames 1 to 4, then tips slightly backward in frame 5. The seated woman bends forward in frame 3, reaching her right hand across the board's top at roughly 0.6 metres from the camera to release a yellow token. She then lowers that arm to her right side in frame 4 and reclines into the couch in frame 5, when the camera wearer's raised left arm partly blocks her right side. Relative to RGB alone, the depth image clearly exposes the metric spacing among the foreground board, the woman's outstretched hand, the couch cushions, and the set-back background walls, whose values become dark beyond 3 to 5 metres. It also recovers depth through several round openings in the grid. Nevertheless, estimates are unreliable inside some small circular Connect Four cutouts, where background depths bleed inconsistently into the foreground plastic, and around the far ceiling grid and recessed hallway, which collapse into an almost uniformly black area.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation image separates the main foreground people and furnishings from an unlabelled background. The woman seated ahead of the camera wearer, approximately 0.9 to 1.3 metres away, faces the camera and looks down at the game; she is identified as a 'person' in every one of the five frames. Sofa cushions behind and to either side of her, about 1.2 to 1.8 metres distant, receive the 'couch' label beginning in frame 2. The Connect Four board at the bottom centre, roughly 0.5 to 0.7 metres away and reachable by either participant, is segmented in frames 3 through 5. During frame 5, the camera wearer's extended left forearm and hand at the lower left, approximately 0.2 to 0.4 metres away, become a second 'person' instance. This mask overlaps and partly blocks both the couch on the left and the seated woman's right arm behind the board. Through the five-frame sequence, the woman's 'person' mask moves upward and widens toward the left in frames 3 and 4 as she bends forward and reaches her right arm first over and then alongside the board. The board's bottom mask also enlarges from frame 3 to frame 4 while the camera points downward. Segmentation defines the exterior outlines of the reaching arms, torso, and furniture more cleanly than RGB, where they merge into the visually busy office background, but it has major semantic and edge failures. In every frame, the open vertical zipper and collar opening on the woman's jacket are wrongly classified as a 'tie.' The blue Connect Four grid is incorrectly labelled a 'laptop' in frames 3 to 5 and is not detected at all in frames 1 and 2. Sofa cushions are divided among several 'couch' and 'bed' instances, while the yellow and red game tokens, ceiling, walls, and floor lamp are omitted completely.
pose: The skeleton visualization follows the 2D keypoints of the woman sitting about 0.9 to 1.3 metres ahead of the camera wearer. In all five frames, grouped yellow facial points for the eyes, nose, and ears indicate that her head remains centred and directed toward the camera wearer, with a slight downward angle toward the game space below. Frames 1 and 2 detect only the head landmarks and an almost horizontal yellow segment joining her left and right shoulders because her lower torso and arms are either hidden behind the game board or cropped by the bottom of the image. When she bends forward in frame 3 and comes within reach of the board, approximately 0.6 metres from the camera, the map shows her complete upper-body trapezoid formed by shoulders and hips, her left arm, and her lifted right arm in yellow. A dense set of magenta right-hand landmarks sits immediately above the board's left side, where she is holding the yellow token. In frame 4, her detected right arm travels downward and toward image-left, with the magenta right hand descending to waist height next to the couch cushion. In frame 5, her torso moves backward, and a magenta hand skeleton appears again near her right shoulder. The visualization exposes her head direction, shoulder angle, and the path of her right arm without distracting imagery. However, frame 5 is especially unreliable: no independent body skeleton is assigned to the camera wearer, and the camera wearer's foreground left hand, about 0.3 metres away, is instead merged with the distant woman's right-arm and hand landmarks, roughly 1.1 metres away. The system also fails to detect her torso in frames 1 and 2 and never detects her left hand.
